title: Team Northstar — An Unfolding Story
synopsis: A new cross-functional team has six weeks to improve onboarding. Its strongest voices dominate meetings while work ownership stays unclear.

opening.speaker: Aisha Okafor
opening.title: The Idea That Stops Mid-Sentence
opening.text: Grant interrupts Aisha: “We already tried that.” Aisha stops speaking. Oscar has data but stays quiet, waiting to see what the leader will do.
opening.prompt: How do you intervene without dismissing Grant's experience?

choices.text: Thank Grant for the context, invite Aisha to finish, and ask Oscar for relevant evidence.
choices.reaction: Aisha reenters the discussion, Grant contributes expertise without dominating, and Oscar's data becomes actionable.
choices.coaching: Build norms that make participation safe and useful.

choices.text: Promise to return to Aisha after the meeting without changing how airtime is allocated.
choices.reaction: Meetings remain civil but ownership and participation are still inconsistent.
choices.coaching: A reassuring or incomplete answer may delay an uncomfortable issue, but does not remove responsibility.

choices.text: Let Grant dismiss the idea because he has the longest experience.
choices.reaction: People retreat into departmental positions and customer problems remain hidden.
choices.coaching: Silencing evidence or substituting certainty for verification increases human and operational risk.

ending-strong.speaker: Narrator
ending-strong.title: Ending: Trust and Direction
ending-strong.text: Northstar establishes shared norms, accountable handoffs and evidence-based improvement. The next test shows meaningful customer progress.
ending-strong.reflection: Which observable behaviors made this result possible, and how will you repeat them?

ending-fragile.speaker: Narrator
ending-fragile.title: Ending: A Recoverable Gap
ending-fragile.text: The team recovers partially, but the next handoff is vulnerable until roles and participation become routine.
ending-fragile.reflection: Which assumption or handoff would you revisit before the next decision?

ending-damaged.speaker: Narrator
ending-damaged.title: Ending: A Costly Leadership Pattern
ending-damaged.text: Departments defend their own work, the customer test continues to fail, and the team's purpose is lost in blame.
ending-damaged.reflection: What would you acknowledge, repair and change first to prevent repetition?
